children: NASA is committing another $359 million to help Boeing
get its troubled Starliner spacecraft flying again, giving the program another lifeline after the serious technical problems that derailed its 2024 crewed mission.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said Starliner could return to the International Space Station as soon as December, although the first flight would carry cargo rather than astronauts.
Crewed missions are not expected to resume until 2028.

The timeline highlights how much work remains after Starliner's 2024 mission encountered multiple technical problems and was later classified by NASA as a Type A mishap, the agency's most serious category.
Astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams ultimately remained aboard the space station for about nine months before returning to Earth aboard a SpaceX

NASA expects Starliner upgrades and certification work for new launch vehicles to cost another $359 million. Planned modifications include redesigned valves and seals intended to address some of the spacecraft's reliability problems.
For Boeing, continued NASA support reduces the risk that years of investment in Starliner will simply be abandoned.

But the delayed return to crewed operations also underscores the financial and execution risk still hanging over the program. Boeing has already absorbed substantial Starliner-related charges, making additional development costs and future NASA payments important metrics for investors.
NASA has a strategic reason to keep Starliner alive.
The agency has long wanted two independent U.S. systems capable of transporting astronauts to orbit rather than relying entirely on SpaceX.
That gives Boeing another chance to prove Starliner can become a dependable second option.

There could also be a longer-term commercial opportunity. With the International Space Station scheduled to retire around 2031, private orbital stations may eventually need crew transportation services.
But Boeing has to clear a much more immediate hurdle first.
Investors should watch whether Starliner returns to flight in December, whether the redesigned systems perform as intended, and whether NASA remains on track for a crewed return in 2028.
Until then, Starliner remains more of a turnaround project than a dependable earnings contributor.

title: NASA Gives Boeing Starliner $359 Million Lifeline
